issues.description: Four PROC SORT BY lists in the original PDF spell the SAS modifier as decending (cached source lines 596, 987, 1050 and 1416; visually confirmed on original PDF pages 14, 22, 24 and 31). SAS documents DESCENDING as the modifier. Once the code is extracted to an editable text working copy, these four spellings require the exact correction decending → descending; do not alter the archival PDF.

The complete supplied source uses article5, tempBas and outofhere without visible producers; the article-return branch reuses the firm-quarter illiqtemp table whose visible schema lacks the article id/m_date fields consumed later. Several author-prepared dk./store. tables are also read without producers. The RavenPack comment names dk.rp_count_ret but executable code reads store.rp_count_ret, so preserve both namespace references until mapped. One %WT invocation repeats parameter names, so its expansion/output remains unresolved without macro-call behavior evidence. Preserve names and request exact producer/schema/key/history contracts; do not guess replacements.

The package lacks full compatible analysis inputs. The identifiers workbook is only gvkey/datadate; local commercial catalog candidates and bounded one-row probes do not prove required product versions, matching fields, population, history or complete coverage. The supplied code also consumes author-prepared tables whose producers/contracts are absent. Historical Seeking Alpha article, profile/category, text and comment/like data need compatible 2006–2018 records and ID links.

SAS, Perl and Stata programs are embedded in a PDF rather than supplied as driver-ready files. The actual order must interleave SAS article preparation, the Perl-generated text CSV, and later SAS import/join. Perl writes a C: path while SAS imports the same-named CSV from a J: path; the SAS remote session/library setup is not shown; and the separate Stata table branches begin without a visible input load/export contract. SAS macros dupl, trading_days and WT are fully defined in the PDF and are not missing merely because they are not standalone files.
